prompt: Wrap a PriceService in a dynamic Proxy that caches each result per method-and-arguments, so a repeated call never reaches the real service. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A dynamic proxy funnels every interface method into one InvocationHandler, which makes it the natural place to add a cross-cutting concern such as caching. The cache key must identify the method as well as the arguments, because priceOf("A") and total("A", 3) are different calls that would otherwise collide; method.getName() plus Arrays.toString(args) gives a cheap, correct key here. containsKey rather than a null check matters once a cached value can itself be null. The real service never learns it is being cached -- that is the whole point of the pattern.
hints: Declare the Map before the call to Proxy.newProxyInstance so the lambda captures it; a local variable used inside a lambda must be effectively final, and a Map reference you only mutate qualifies.
The handler receives (proxy, method, args). Build the key from method.getName() and Arrays.toString(args) -- note that args is null for a no-argument method, which Arrays.toString handles.
On a cache miss call method.invoke(target, args), put the result under the key, and return it. Never call method.invoke(proxy, args) -- that would loop forever.
